newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli firms in suit over Lucent representation.
newsitem.headline: Israeli firms in suit over Lucent representation.

text.p: The former representative in Israel of AT&T's microelectronics division, now known as Lucent Technologies, is suing the new representative for $1 million, documents filed in Tel Aviv District Court show.

The privately held SMD Electronics Ltd was the representative for ATT Microelectronics division for several years until January 1996, when it was replaced by Vectronics, a subsidiary of Rada Electronic Industries Ltd.
ATT Corp recently spun off telecom equipment maker Lucent in a three-way split of the telecommunciations giant.
In the suit, SMD claims that Vectronics agreed in writing to pay it $1 million for transferring the representation.

The lawsuit is expected to take more than two years to be heard. But in preliminary proceedings, SMD managing director Issac Gilmore on Thursday filed an affidavit in response to an one filed by Lucent. In the document he alleges a breach of contract on the part of AT&T Microelectronics.
David Mahal, head of Vectronics, denied all the allegations. "We did not commit ourselves to pay $1 million," he told Reuters.
